clue.text: Officially approved drug charge

parts.note: a document that is officially approved has been stamped
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A police officer files a charge for drug dealing that has been officially signed off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a criminal charge; the answer is a charge in the sense of a headlong rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden mass rush forward, which is one sense of a charge by animals or troops.

clue.text: See 14
Talk more excitedly about wife's artisanal craft

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters wrap the next piece
talking excitedly jumbles things up, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone gushes about their wife's handmade crafts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk more' reads as the verb of the sentence, but it is only the raw material for the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Metalwork is the skilled making of objects from metal, a traditional hand trade practised by smiths and artisans.

clue.text: Nationalist extremists carrying Britain's status post-Brexit in dramatic direction

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is carried sits on top, so the second piece goes above the first

parts.note: after Brexit Britain is ex-EU, a former member of the European Union

indicators.note: the extremists of a word are its two end letters, its first and last

parts.note: the first and last letters of Nationalist

explanation.surface: Political extremists are blamed for Britain's dramatic change of direction after Brexit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the carried piece rides on top. The answer is the Latin stage direction meaning 'they go out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is a stage instruction in play scripts telling several actors to leave, so it is literally a direction in drama.

clue.text: Annexed enclave includes biblical location

indicators.note: the words before it contain the required letters running across them

parts.note: found inside the end of annexed and the start of enclave

explanation.surface: A territory that has been annexed turns out to contain a site mentioned in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the garden where Genesis places Adam and Eve, a place named in the Bible.

clue.text: Medieval weapon originally appearing after 1000 AD

indicators.note: after places the following letters behind the Roman numeral piece

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: first letter of appearing
CE, Common Era, is the modern equivalent of AD

explanation.surface: A historian notes that a certain medieval weapon first turned up after the year 1000.
explanation.walkthrough: AD is not taken literally: it is swapped for its modern equivalent CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy club with a spiked or flanged metal head, used by knights in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Imitator of Apple product that's adorable

parts.note: the Mac is Apple's line of computers
aw is the cooing sound people make at something cute

explanation.surface: Someone copies an Apple gadget and everyone coos over how cute it is.
explanation.walkthrough: Imitator looks like a knock-off maker, but it defines a parrot that mimics speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large parrot, and parrots are famous mimics of human speech and sounds.

clue.text: Song and dance halved, and cheers doubled

indicators.note: halved means only half of the dance's name is kept
and joins the two pieces one after the other

parts.note: the cancan is a high-kicking French dance
ta is an informal British thanks, as is cheers, and it is written twice

explanation.surface: A show offers half a dance routine and a double helping of applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a vocal composition for singers and instruments, so it is a sung musical work.

clue.text: Alert newlywed vacated during catastrophic toast

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece goes inside the other
a catastrophic toast has gone badly wrong, so its letters are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: a vacated word has been emptied of its middle, keeping only its ends

parts.note: first and last letters of newlywed

explanation.surface: A newlywed has to stay alert when the wedding toast goes horribly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: TOAST becomes STA TO with ND placed in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Stand-to is the military state of readiness when soldiers take up positions, as at dawn, a call to be on alert.

clue.text: Colonising group, the European migrants initially in temporary accommodation

definitions.note: a gerund used as a noun; the answer is the act of colonising

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the shelter that follows

parts.note: a set is a group
a tent is a short-term shelter
le is the French for the, a European word for it

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of migrants

explanation.surface: A group of European migrants is housed in temporary camps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonising group' looks like a single definition, but colonising alone defines the answer and group is wordplay. The French article counts as a European 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Settlement means the act of settling people in a new territory, which is exactly what colonising involves.

clue.text: Give a Fig Newton for recipe as source of sugar

indicators.note: X for Y means put X where Y was, swapping one letter in

parts.note: to give a fig is to care, as in 'I don't give a fig'
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force
R is the abbreviation for recipe on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone passes off a Fig Newton biscuit as the sweet part of a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Fig Newton reads as a biscuit, but it splits into Fig and Newton. N replaces the R in CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar cane is a tall grass whose stems are crushed to extract most of the world's sugar.

clue.text: Spouse's song describing new husband absorbed by first child

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the song goes round the next letter

parts.note: a ballad is a song
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken inside, so the first piece goes into the second

parts.note: Cain was the first son of Adam and Eve
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife sings about her new husband being taken up with their firstborn.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes into BALLAD for BALLAND, and H goes into CAIN for CHAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball and chain is jokey slang for a wife or husband, picturing marriage as a prisoner's shackle.

clue.text: Frosty perhaps, sun presently starts to materialise around noon

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday
presently can mean at the present time

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words are their first letters

parts.note: first letters of materialise, around and noon

explanation.surface: A weather report: frost possible, the sun starting to come out around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Frosty is not weather but the name of a famous character from a Christmas song.
explanation.definitionFit: Frosty the Snowman is the title figure of a popular Christmas song, an example of a figure built from snow.

clue.text: Priest meeting holy texts' writer

indicators.note: meeting puts the two pieces side by side, one after the other

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword favourite
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A priest meets the author of some sacred scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is George Eliot or T.S. Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot the novelist and T.S. Eliot the poet are both famous authors bearing this surname.

clue.text: Hot, newly broadcast US season includes kind of documentary

indicators.note: includes means the season's name holds the jumbled letters inside it

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so the words before it are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A TV listing: a hot new American series featuring a documentary.
explanation.walkthrough: HOT NEWLY is rearranged and placed after the F of FALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly-on-the-wall films observe their subjects unobtrusively without narration, a recognised style of observational documentary.

clue.text: Billionaire? Idiot carrying unreasonable clout

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the idiot wraps around the other letters

parts.note: prat is British slang for a fool

indicators.note: something unreasonable is out of order, so the word after it is rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A jibe at a billionaire: a fool wielding unreasonable influence.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is someone whose power comes from great wealth, so a billionaire is a typical instance.

clue.text: Opener part of Ireland's team

parts.note: Cork is a county and city in Ireland
the possessive ending kept as it is
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: An opening player in an Irish sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: Opener suggests a sports batsman, but it means a tool for opening bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the spiral tool used to pull corks out of wine bottles, so it opens them.

clue.text: Engineering student failing his essential GCSE

parts.note: Eng is the abbreviation for engineering

indicators.note: failing suggests breaking down, so the word beside it is rearranged

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineering student fails one of his compulsory school exams.
explanation.walkthrough: GCSEs are the exams English pupils take at about 16, and English is a compulsory subject.
explanation.definitionFit: English language is one of the core subjects every pupil sits at GCSE, the standard exam at age sixteen.

clue.text: Running after detectives apprehending popular poet

indicators.note: after puts the first-named piece at the end
detectives apprehending someone take them in, so they hold the next piece

parts.note: dick is old American slang for a detective
in means fashionable or popular
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: Detectives chase down and arrest a well-loved poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Dickinson was a celebrated nineteenth-century American poet, known for short lyrics full of dashes.

clue.text: Playwright's changed since winning Oscar upon Oscar

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters that follow are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet, given twice

explanation.surface: A playwright has been transformed after winning one Oscar after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugène Ionesco was a Romanian-French dramatist, a leading figure of the Theatre of the Absurd.

clue.text: Smell one primarily associated with earlier memory

indicators.note: earlier puts the memory piece in front of the letter just chosen

parts.note: a means one
ROM is read-only memory in a computer

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, picking the opening letter

parts.note: first letter of associated

explanation.surface: A scent is most closely linked with an old memory.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive, usually pleasant odour, so it is a kind of smell.

clue.text: Copper plated with light element

indicators.note: plated with means covered by a layer, so the second piece surrounds the first

parts.note: light-hearted, cheerful
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: copper coated with a lightweight element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' tempts towards hydrogen or helium, but here it means cheerful, as in light-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is a chemical element, the metal that is liquid at room temperature.

clue.text: Relatively plain creature, cold, lacking in beauty, hollow even

indicators.note: lacking in means without, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a peach is a beauty, something very attractive
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: a hollow word is emptied of its middle, leaving only its ends

parts.note: first and last letters of even

explanation.surface: A dowdy animal, frosty and short on looks, even empty inside.
explanation.walkthrough: C is removed from PEACH, leaving PEAH.
explanation.definitionFit: The peahen is the female peafowl, drab brown beside the dazzling peacock, so plain by comparison.

clue.text: Famous houses succumbed to strain without leader to initiate work

indicators.note: houses means holds inside, so the first word wraps the second

parts.note: famous means well known

indicators.note: without its leader means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: something that buckled gave way under pressure

explanation.surface: Famous buildings collapsed under the weight of an unwilling workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houses' looks like buildings, but it is the verb meaning holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To knuckle down is to start applying oneself seriously to a task, getting stuck in to the job.

clue.text: See 11
Change in Romania certain to bring about unemployment

parts.note: the leu, plural lei, is Romania's currency, and change means coins
sure means certain

explanation.surface: An economist predicts that reform in Romania is bound to cause joblessness.
explanation.walkthrough: Change looks like reform, but it means small money: Romanian coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is time free from work, and unemployment in its literal sense is simply not being occupied.

clue.text: Drink noisily, not quietly, and speak drunkenly

indicators.note: not means the letter for the following word is taken out

parts.note: to slurp is to drink with a sucking noise
p is piano, the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A drunk gulps loudly, can't keep quiet, and mumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: To slur is to run words together indistinctly, the classic mark of someone who has had too much drink.

clue.text: The East Australian singer preceded by amateur

indicators.note: preceded by puts the later-named piece in front

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for amateur
Sia is the Australian pop singer-songwriter

explanation.surface: An Australian singer tours the East, with an amateur opening the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the continent traditionally meant by the East or the Orient in Western usage.

clue.text: Returning and briefly dwelling around old city with hellish odour

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: plus means and

indicators.note: around means the shortened dwelling surrounds the city
briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a house is a dwelling
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: Coming back to an old town's house to find it reeking of brimstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a mere joining word, but it stands for its mathematical synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulphur, the biblical brimstone, burns with a choking stench linked with hell, so sulphurous describes that infernal smell.

clue.text: See 23
Unwary as desperate fugitives

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild and frantic, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Escapees on the run grow careless when desperate.
explanation.definitionFit: Runaways are people who have fled, from home or custody, so they are escapees on the run.
